changes.before: Use an empty int array with the same total initialization. What prints?
changes.after: Add array items by visiting each one in order.

before: for (int value : values) visits the array elements in order and assigns each primitive value to the local loop variable for that pass.
total = total + value updates the accumulator. It does not alter the source array.
Assigning a new int to value would not rewrite its array slot. To replace a slot, use the array and an index explicitly.
If the array has no elements, the loop body runs zero times and an accumulator initialized to zero stays zero.
Expected output or behavior: 12. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.

Optional local transfer task: Trace an empty array and a one-element array. Then explain why changing a copied int loop variable would not update the array. You may trace it without a JDK; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
after: An enhanced for loop visits each item in an array. On each turn here, Java copies the next integer into the local variable value. You do not need to manage an index.
A running total keeps the sum so far. Each turn adds value to total and stores the new sum back in total. This leaves the array unchanged.
value holds a copy of an integer. Assigning a different integer to value would change only that local variable. To replace an array item, assign through the array's index.
An empty array has no items to visit. The loop body runs zero times, so the starting total stays unchanged.
The program prints 12. The running total moves from zero to two, then six, then twelve.
The quiz keeps the starting total but removes the array's items. Decide whether any instruction inside the loop can now run.

before.question: Use an empty int array with the same total initialization. What prints?
choices: 12 because the previous example is remembered.
An exception because every enhanced for needs an element.
0 because no visit changes the initial total.
before.explanation: The empty array contributes no iterations.

after.question: Use an empty int array and keep total starting at zero. What prints?
choices: 12, because Java remembers the old array.
An error, because this loop needs at least one item.
0, because the loop never changes the starting total.
after.explanation: There are no items to visit, so the body never runs and total stays zero.
